final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the interpretation of the same record. That clarification is substantively aligned with the initial concern: rollout controls, aggregate readiness, and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents are supportive operational facts, but they are not sufficient for policy compliance when a named launch use case remains materially exposed. The governing policy and case-specific policy text require either exclusion of the affected use case, approved risk acceptance covering that exposure, or fulfillment of the disclosure duty. The admissible evidence shows the opposite of the first two predicates and does not prove the third: the exposed segment remains in scope for rollout, the risk acceptance is incomplete and unapproved, and no final model-card or equivalent launch disclosure is in evidence. Because the unresolved issue is a missing compliance predicate rather than merely an overbroad phrasing problem, the narrowed caveat is not enough to reach compliant_with_caveats on this record. The appropriate final assessment remains suspicious, with escalation warranted until evidence of the actual policy-satisfying path is produced.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required pre-launch disclosure was actually completed for the exposed emergency shelter placement use case.
The affected emergency shelter placement segment remains below target and remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort.
Rollout controls do not exclude the affected use case, so monitoring, rollback, and limited initial percentage do not satisfy the policy predicate by themselves.
The risk acceptance document is only a draft, has no approval, and does not address the exposed emergency shelter placement use case.
The record still lacks a certification basis showing which permitted policy path was actually used before launch.
